findings.where: comparison bars for Claude 3.5 and GPT-4o

findings.before: Light grey 2px bars on a pale track
findings.after: Bars at #767676 or darker, 4px+ thick, with the track removed or lightened
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: graphical objects that carry data need 3:1.
findings.title: Large text, icons, focus rings, field edges, control boundaries, data marks.

findings.evidence: Comparator scores are implausible for the named models: "Claude 3.5 88.2" and "GPT-4o 83.6" on AIME 2025, when those models are publicly reported far lower on AIME. findings.why: Unsourced, likely invented competitor numbers turn a benchmark slide into fabricated proof; the insight line's margins inherit the error.
findings.title: Never invent a metric, customer count, uptime, speed multiple, saving or percentage the us

findings.evidence: Failed T-GHOST-DECK / T-SO-WHAT: the title "Coding Capability Breakthrough." is a label any model launch could use (T-RIVAL-NAME holds for any vendor), while the assertion "open-source models can compete at the frontier ... margins of +7.5 to +20.5 points" is 13px grey text at the bottom-left.
findings.after: Promote the claim to the title, e.g. "GLM-4.7 leads all three coding benchmarks by 7.5 to 20.5 points" (once the comparators are sourced)
findings.why: Read as a ghost deck, the title says nothing only this slide can say; the point is in the smallest text.
findings.title: Make slide titles full declarative assertions, unique per slide

findings.evidence: Wide-tracked uppercase micro labels: "GLM-4.7 OPEN-SOURCE MODEL" (10px, letter-spaced), "ZHIPU AI" preceded by a terracotta hairline rule, plus tracked caps metric names "SWE-BENCH VERIFIED". T-DELETION: the eyebrow repeats what the title and figures already say.
findings.before: G L M - 4 . 7   O P E N - S O U R C E   M O D E L
findings.after: Drop the eyebrow; put "GLM-4.7" in the title and the source in a legible footer line
findings.why: Tracked-caps eyebrows and the rule-plus-wordmark sign-off are the stock 'luxury slide' kit.
findings.title: No eyebrow labels above headings
findings.fix: Promote any fact into the heading or the line below it; delete the rest.

findings.evidence: Terracotta (#d4a574) dot replaces the decimal point in "95.7", "73.8", "87.4" and ends the title "Breakthrough."; with the off-white ground and caps eyebrows this is 3 tells of the warm-paper family (terracotta_accent, eyebrows, near-cream ground) on one slide. The sweep did not cluster it because the display face is sans.
findings.after: Plain decimals in the figure colour; spend the single accent only on the GLM-4.7 rows, where it encodes 'ours'
findings.why: An ornamental accent on punctuation is decoration; the accent already has a job in the bars.
findings.title: Look-family cluster
findings.fix: Break the family on its strongest tell first; name the replacement decision.

findings.evidence: dom-1920 text for the first figure is "957" with the decimal point in a separate decorative span; if the dot span is hidden or styled as a glyph, the value is extracted as 957, not 95.7.
findings.after: Keep the real '.' character in the figure's text and colour it via a span that stays in the text flow, or add aria-label="95.7" on the figure
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: copied or exported text must keep the value.
findings.title: Keep all words as real text in reading order

findings.evidence: dom-1920: no heading elements; the title "Coding Capability Breakthrough." is div.main-title and metric names are divs; no landmarks.
findings.after: <h1 class="main-title"> and <h2> for each benchmark name, so PDF export tags and screen readers get an outline
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; matters once the slide is exported to tagged PDF (SLD-105).
findings.title: Use landmarks and semantic elements

findings.where: vertical bands at 1920x1080: y 220-430 and y 700-930
